what: Example A: Logistic regression (DVT diagnosis model)
title: Guide for Model Developers
text: DVT example dataset included package spans seven studies. Studies 1-5 used model development; studies 6-7 reserved external validation. writes dvt_v1/dvt_v1_specification.json. coefficient values protected; file safe host GitHub repository.
code: dvt_path <- system.file("extdata", "dvt_example.csv", package = "evaluatr") dvt_data <- read.csv(dvt_path)  # Development set: studies 1-5 dvt_dev <- dvt_data[dvt_data$study %in% 1:5, ]  # Fit a logistic regression model dvt_fit <- glm(dvt ~ male + ab_ddimer + calf_diff + vein_distension +                      malignancy + immobile,                data = dvt_dev, family = binomial)  # Generate the protected model specification file register_model(   model           = dvt_fit,   model_id        = "dvt_v1",   developer_id    = "your-github-username",    # your GitHub username   model_name      = "DVT Diagnosis Model v1",   description     = paste(     "Logistic regression for DVT diagnosis. Developed in studies 1-5",     "of the simulated DVT example dataset.",     "Predictors: male, ab_ddimer, calf_diff, vein_distension, malignancy, immobile."   ),   developer_name  = "Your Name",   developer_email = "you@institution.ac.uk",   output_dir      = "dvt_v1" )

what: Example B: Cox proportional hazards model (breast cancer relapse)
title: Guide for Model Developers
text: Cox models, model_parameters must include timepoints baseline_survival evaluatr can produce predicted survival probabilities specific time-points.
code: library(survival)  bc_path <- system.file("extdata", "bc_survival_example.csv",                        package = "evaluatr") bc_data <- read.csv(bc_path) bc_dev  <- bc_data[bc_data$val == 0, ]  # Fit a Cox model cox_fit <- coxph(Surv(rf, rfi) ~ age + nodes + pr + er + hormon,                  data = bc_dev, x = TRUE)  # Extract baseline survival at 5 and 10 years (60 and 120 months) bh     <- basehaz(cox_fit, centered = FALSE) S0_60  <- exp(-bh$hazard[which.min(abs(bh$time - 60))]) S0_120 <- exp(-bh$hazard[which.min(abs(bh$time - 120))])  register_model(   model            = cox_fit,   model_id         = "bc_cox_v1",   developer_id     = "your-github-username",   model_name       = "Breast Cancer Relapse-Free Survival Model",   description      = paste(     "Cox PH model for relapse-free survival in breast cancer.",     "Developed in the training set (val == 0) of the bc_survival_example dataset.",     "Predictors: age, nodes, pr, er, hormon."   ),   model_parameters = list(     timepoints        = c(60, 120),     baseline_survival = c(S0_60, S0_120)   ),   developer_name  = "Your Name",   developer_email = "you@institution.ac.uk",   output_dir      = "bc_cox_v1" )

title: Guide for Evaluators
text: example uses DVT diagnosis dataset included package, validated logistic regression model hosted public evaluatr demo repository. illustrates complete evaluatr workflow binary outcome model, can run exactly written — developer contact required. result object contains shuffled prediction-outcome matrix. shuffling means predictions matched back individual patient rows, ensures package used generate predictions individual patients clinical practice. metrics table includes following:
code: library(evaluatr)  # Load the DVT example dataset dvt_path <- system.file("extdata", "dvt_example.csv", package = "evaluatr") dvt_data <- read.csv(dvt_path)  # Use studies 6 and 7 as the external validation set # (studies 1-5 were used for model development) dvt_val <- dvt_data[dvt_data$study %in% c(6, 7), ]  # Run secure validation against the public evaluatr demo model. # The token below is a shared public demo credential (not a real GitHub # token) for demonstration purposes only. In real use, the model developer # provides you with a private-repo GitHub token. result <- secure_model_validation(   repo_owner      = "JoieEnsor",   repo_name       = "evaluatr-demo-models",   model_id        = "dvt_logistic_v1",   github_token    = "evaluatr-demo",   validation_data = dvt_val,   outcome         = "dvt" ) # Compute performance metrics performance <- eval_performance(   validation_result    = result,   generate_plots       = TRUE,   confidence_intervals = TRUE,   n_boot               = 50,      # low here for illustration purposes   decision_threshold   = 0.15     # set to the clinically relevant threshold )  # View the metrics table performance$metrics  # Access individual diagnostic plots performance$plots$calibration      # calibration plot performance$plots$decision_curve   # decision curve analysis performance$plots$distribution     # predicted probability distributions

title: Guide for Evaluators
text: Many validation studies assess model performance separately within clinically relevant subgroups, sex, age group, recruitment site. evaluatr supports argument. workflow two stages. First, pass secure_model_validation() subgroup label retained alongside shuffled prediction. Second, pass result$shuffled_by eval_performance() obtain separate metrics per subgroup. subgroup must contain least 50 observations. subgroup smaller , secure_model_validation() return informative error predictions computed.
code: # Stage 1 — run validation retaining study labels result_by_study <- secure_model_validation(   repo_owner      = "developer-username",   repo_name       = "my-models",   model_id        = "dvt_v1",   github_token    = "token_provided_by_developer",   validation_data = dvt_val,   outcome         = "dvt",   by              = "study"     # column name in your dataset )  # Stage 2 — compute metrics separately per study performance_by_study <- eval_performance(   validation_result    = result_by_study,   generate_plots       = TRUE,   confidence_intervals = TRUE,   n_boot               = 50,      # low here for illustration purposes   decision_threshold   = 0.15,   by                   = result_by_study$shuffled_by )  # The metrics table now has a Subgroup column performance_by_study$metrics  # Plots are organised by subgroup level performance_by_study$plots[["6"]]$calibration   # study 6 performance_by_study$plots[["7"]]$calibration   # study 7

what: evaluatr: Secure Independent Evaluation of Clinical Prediction Models — evaluatr-package
title: evaluatr: Secure Independent Evaluation of Clinical Prediction Models — evaluatr-package
text: evaluatr package implements two-component system independent external validation clinical prediction algorithms, designed simultaneously satisfy: Scientific rigour – fully independent evaluators complete control data reporting. Commercial viability – model coefficients never leave developer's private GitHub repository. Data sovereignty – patient data never leaves evaluator's secure local environment.

title: evaluatr: Secure Independent Evaluation of Clinical Prediction Models — evaluatr-package
text: model developer uses register_model() create protected model specification registers model evaluatr registry. specification uploaded private GitHub repository. developer issues time-limited, fine-grained access token evaluator. evaluator calls secure_model_validation() local dataset developer-provided token. Predictions computed entirely within evaluator's R session; output shuffled prediction-outcome matrix. evaluator passes result eval_performance() obtain discrimination, calibration, utility metrics optional bootstrap confidence intervals diagnostic plots.

title: evaluatr: Secure Independent Evaluation of Clinical Prediction Models — evaluatr-package
text: Model coefficients protected rest transit; never exposed readable R objects. Predictions cleared memory returned. returned matrix row-shuffled predictions matched back individual patient records. minimum dataset size 50 observations (per subgroup) enforced prevent near-individual prediction coefficient reverse-engineering. Every validation event logged evaluatr registry.

title: evaluatr: Secure Independent Evaluation of Clinical Prediction Models — evaluatr-package
text: Three example datasets included package: dvt_example – simulated DVT diagnosis dataset, 9,805 patients across seven studies (binary outcome). Loaded via read.csv(system.file("extdata", "dvt_example.csv",     package = "evaluatr")). bc_survival_example – breast cancer relapse-free survival dataset, 2,232 patients pre-assigned development/validation split (survival outcome). Loaded via read.csv(system.file("extdata", "bc_survival_example.csv",     package = "evaluatr")). adnex_sample – de-identified ADNEX ovarian cancer validation dataset, 1,500 patients (multinomial outcome). Loaded via readRDS(system.file("extdata", "adnex_sample.rds",     package = "evaluatr")).

code: eval_performance(   validation_result,   generate_plots = TRUE,   confidence_intervals = TRUE,   n_boot = 200,   plot_title = NULL,   decision_threshold = 0.1,   by = NULL,   cal_args = list(),   dca_args = list() )

title: Calculate Performance Metrics from a Validation Result — eval_performance
text: validation_result List. Output secure_model_validation(). generate_plots Logical. Whether produce calibration, decision curve, probability distribution plots. Default TRUE. confidence_intervals Logical. Whether compute 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Default TRUE. n_boot Integer. Number bootstrap resamples. Default 200. Increase 1000 publication-quality confidence intervals. plot_title Character NULL. Optional title suffix added plot headings. decision_threshold Numeric. Probability threshold used net benefit calculations decision curve. Default 0.1. Set clinically relevant threshold outcome. Vector NULL. Optional subgroup vector length predictions (pass result$shuffled_by output secure_model_validation() argument). provided, metrics computed separately level variable. cal_args Named list additional arguments controlling calibration plot. Supported options: g Integer. Number groups. Default 10. smooth Character. Flexible calibration curve method: "loess" (default) "rcs". CL.smooth Whether show confidence band around flexible curve: "fill" (default shaded band), "line", FALSE suppress. xlim Numeric vector length 2. X-axis limits. Default c(0, 1). ylim Numeric vector length 2. Y-axis limits. Default c(0, 1). dca_args Named list additional arguments controlling decision curve analysis. Supported options: thresholds Numeric vector. Threshold probabilities evaluate net benefit. Default seq(0, 1, = 0.01). standardize Logical. TRUE, plot standardised net benefit instead net benefit. Default FALSE. policy Character. "opt-" (default, treat high-risk patients) "opt-" (withhold treatment low-risk patients).

title: Calculate Performance Metrics from a Validation Result — eval_performance
text: named list: metrics Data frame performance metrics. supplied Subgroup column prepended. plots List plot objects: calibration, decision_curve, distribution. supplied, plots organised subgroup level: plots[["level_name"]]$calibration, etc. model_info Metadata validation_result. decision_threshold threshold value used. subgroup_variable Name variable (subgroup analysis ). subgroup_categories Character vector category names (subgroup analysis ).

title: Calculate Performance Metrics from a Validation Result — eval_performance
text: Metrics computed include: AUROC/c-statistic, calibration intercept, calibration slope, ECI, ICI, ECE, O:E ratio, Brier score, Nagelkerke R-squared, Cox-Snell R-squared, McFadden R-squared, net benefit, standardised net benefit. function currently supports binary outcomes (0/1) . Multinomial support planned future release.

title: Calculate Performance Metrics from a Validation Result — eval_performance
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # ---- Whole-dataset evaluation ---------------------------------------------- dvt_path <- system.file("extdata", "dvt_example.csv", package = "evaluatr") dvt_val  <- read.csv(dvt_path) dvt_val  <- dvt_val[dvt_val$study %in% c(6, 7), ]  result <- secure_model_validation(   repo_owner      = "JoieEnsor",   repo_name       = "evaluatr-demo-models",   model_id        = "dvt_logistic_v1",   github_token    = "evaluatr-demo",   validation_data = dvt_val,   outcome         = "dvt" )  perf <- eval_performance(   result,   n_boot             = 200,   decision_threshold = 0.15 ) perf$metrics  # Access individual diagnostic plots perf$plots$calibration    # calibration plot perf$plots$decision_curve # decision curve analysis perf$plots$distribution   # predicted probability distribution  # ---- Subgroup evaluation by study ----------------------------------------- result_by_study <- secure_model_validation(   repo_owner      = "JoieEnsor",   repo_name       = "evaluatr-demo-models",   model_id        = "dvt_logistic_v1",   github_token    = "evaluatr-demo",   validation_data = dvt_val,   outcome         = "dvt",   by              = "study" )  perf_by_study <- eval_performance(   result_by_study,   by                 = result_by_study$shuffled_by,   n_boot             = 200,   decision_threshold = 0.15 )  # Metrics table has a Subgroup column perf_by_study$metrics  # Access study-specific plots perf_by_study$plots[["6"]]$calibration perf_by_study$plots[["7"]]$calibration  # ---- Customising the calibration plot ------------------------------------- perf_custom <- eval_performance(   result,   n_boot             = 200,   decision_threshold = 0.15,   cal_args = list(smooth = "rcs", g = 5),   dca_args = list(standardize = TRUE) ) } # }

code: register_model(   model = NULL,   coefficients = NULL,   model_type = NULL,   model_id = NULL,   developer_id = NULL,   model_name = NULL,   outcome_type = NULL,   variables = NULL,   description = "",   version = "1.0",   preprocessing = NULL,   model_parameters = NULL,   reference_category = NULL,   registrant_relationship = NULL,   developer_name = NULL,   developer_email = NULL,   public_listing = TRUE,   rate_limit_exempt = FALSE,   output_dir = "." )

title: Register a model and generate its protected specification file — register_model
text: model fitted model object. Supported classes: glm (binomial family), coxph, survreg (Weibull/exponential), multinom (nnet). Exactly one model coefficients must non-NULL. coefficients named numeric vector (flat models) named list named numeric vectors (multinomial, one entry per non-reference category). Exactly one model coefficients must non-NULL. model_type Character. Required coefficients supplied. One "logistic", "cox", "weibull", "multinomial". model_id Character. Unique identifier model (required). Must match folder name GitHub repository (e.g. "dvt_v1"). Choose name meaningful unlikely conflict developers' models. developer_id Character. identifier (e.g. GitHub username). Used attribute model evaluatr registry (required). model_name Character. Human-readable name (required). outcome_type Character. One "binary", "survival", "multinomial". Required coefficients supplied; inferred automatically model objects. variables Character vector predictor variable names (including "(Intercept)"). Required coefficients supplied; inferred model objects. description Character. Free-text description model. Default "". Recommended: include outcome definition, predictor list, development dataset used. version Character. Version string. Default "1.0". preprocessing Character NULL. R code string evaluated evaluator's validation_data prediction (e.g. create derived variables dummy columns). Default NULL. code must modify validation_data place; access object nothing else. model_parameters Named list NULL. Additional parameters required Cox Weibull models: Cox: list(timepoints = c(...), baseline_survival = c(...)) Weibull: list(timepoints = c(...), shape = <value>, parameterisation = "aft"). shape parameter extracted automatically survreg objects can overridden . reference_category Character NULL. multinomial models: name reference category (category whose coefficients zero). Required model_type = "multinomial" coefficients supplied. Inferred automatically multinom objects. registrant_relationship Character. Required. relationship model registered. Must one "original_developer" (created model), "authorised_proxy" (registering behalf original developer permission), "independent" (registering model developed others). stored evaluatr registry used endorsement decisions. developer_name Character NULL. name (e.g. "Jane Smith"). Stored evaluatr registry evaluators can identify model maintainer. Optional recommended. developer_email Character NULL. Contact email evaluators wish request validation token. Optional strongly recommended want model discoverable via list_registered_models(). public_listing Logical. Whether list model public evaluatr registry (returned list_registered_models()). Default TRUE. Set FALSE keep registration private paper review, example. rate_limit_exempt Logical. Whether model exempt key-fetch rate limit. Default FALSE. Set TRUE demo/ teaching models intended open repeated use. Also useful fully open access models e.g., specification already published open access. output_dir Character. Directory write specification file. Created exist. Default ".". file written {model_id}_specification.json inside directory.

title: Register a model and generate its protected specification file — register_model
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # ---- Example 1: Logistic regression (DVT diagnosis model) ------------------ dvt_path <- system.file("extdata", "dvt_example.csv", package = "evaluatr") dvt_data <- read.csv(dvt_path)  # Fit on development studies 1-5 dvt_dev <- dvt_data[dvt_data$study %in% 1:5, ] dvt_fit <- glm(dvt ~ male + ab_ddimer + calf_diff + vein_distension +                      malignancy + immobile,                data = dvt_dev, family = binomial)  register_model(   model          = dvt_fit,   model_id       = "dvt_v1",   developer_id   = "your-github-username",   model_name     = "DVT Diagnosis Model v1",   description    = "Logistic regression for DVT diagnosis, developed in studies 1-5.",   developer_name  = "Your Name",   developer_email = "you@institution.ac.uk",   output_dir     = "dvt_v1" ) # Upload dvt_v1/dvt_v1_specification.json to your private GitHub repository.  # ---- Example 2: Cox survival model (breast cancer relapse) ---------------- bc_path <- system.file("extdata", "bc_survival_example.csv",                        package = "evaluatr") bc_data <- read.csv(bc_path) bc_dev  <- bc_data[bc_data$val == 0, ]  library(survival) cox_fit <- coxph(Surv(rf, rfi) ~ age + nodes + pr + er + hormon,                  data = bc_dev, x = TRUE)  # Baseline survival at 5 and 10 years (months: 60 and 120) bh <- basehaz(cox_fit, centered = FALSE) S0_60  <- exp(-bh$hazard[which.min(abs(bh$time - 60))]) S0_120 <- exp(-bh$hazard[which.min(abs(bh$time - 120))])  register_model(   model            = cox_fit,   model_id         = "bc_cox_v1",   developer_id     = "your-github-username",   model_name       = "Breast Cancer Relapse-Free Survival Model",   description      = "Cox PH model for relapse-free survival, development set.",   model_parameters = list(     timepoints         = c(60, 120),     baseline_survival  = c(S0_60, S0_120)   ),   developer_name  = "Your Name",   developer_email = "you@institution.ac.uk",   output_dir      = "bc_cox_v1" )  # ---- Example 3: Manual coefficients (logistic) ---------------------------- register_model(   coefficients = c("(Intercept)" = -3.2, ab_ddimer = 1.8,                    calf_diff = 1.1, vein_distension = 0.9),   model_type   = "logistic",   model_id     = "dvt_manual_v1",   developer_id = "your-github-username",   model_name   = "DVT Manual Coefficients",   outcome_type = "binary",   variables    = c("ab_ddimer", "calf_diff", "vein_distension"),   output_dir   = "dvt_manual_v1" ) } # }

title: Secure Model Validation — secure_model_validation
text: repo_owner Character. GitHub username organisation owning model repository. repo_name Character. Name GitHub repository containing model specification. model_id Character. Unique identifier model (must match folder name models/ repository). github_token Character. Fine-grained GitHub personal access token read-access repository. Provided model developer. validation_data Data frame. evaluator's local dataset, must contain predictor variables required model. outcome Character. Name outcome variable validation_data. title: Secure Model Validation — secure_model_validation
text: named list class evaluatr_result containing: shuffled_outcome_predictions Matrix shuffled outcome-prediction pairs (subgroup column specified). shuffled_outcomes Numeric vector shuffled outcomes. shuffled_predictions Numeric vector shuffled predicted probabilities (binary models ). shuffled_by Vector shuffled subgroup values (present specified). prediction_matrix Matrix shuffled predicted probabilities (multinomial models: one column per outcome category). model_info List model metadata including model_id, model_name, model_type, version, required_variables, n_predictions, validation_timestamp.

title: Secure Model Validation — secure_model_validation
text: minimum dataset size enforced (per subgroup used). Predictions shuffled returned matched back individual patient records, preventing reverse-engineering model coefficients ensuring system used make predictions individual patients clinical practice. Patient data never transmitted outside R session. validation event logged evaluatr registry. use function need four items model developer: GitHub username, repository name, model ID, time-limited access token. See evaluator guide vignette (vignette("evaluator-guide", package = "evaluatr")) step--step walkthrough. Use list_registered_models() browse publicly registered models find developer contact details.
